items.title: Henry Johnson interviewed by Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 30, 1995
items.q: That’s what made Ahmad Jamal so great and Oscar Peterson, you know?

ctx.x: I want to ask you, can you delineate for us if I’m having some students that are going to be watching this video. Tell us some differences between, like in terms of your tone quality and of the volume, and maybe even what you do in the left hand, between jazz guitar playing and rock guitar playing. Now I will tell you this. I met a rock guitar player. I was in a music store trying out an instrument and he was in there kind of banging away with big bar chords and stuff. And I told him, you know, you need to listen…

Well, jazz is like to me it’s probably the ultimate music to play because it’s the type of music that you can find your own identity in. Rock & roll, they use a lot of the loud guitars, and a lot of distortion. And the distortion is exactly what it says, it distorts the tone. So with jazz I’m looking for the purest tone I can get. Because that’s going to allow my own identity to come out in that in the dynamics. When I work with Joe, and playing jazz on my own, the music to me has to have peaks and valleys.…

beat. I can do all of those things just by doing this with my hand and my arm. But the rock players, they just crank it up and that’s where it is. And it stays that way the whole night. Pounding, pounding, pounding your ear. And to me, music should caress you and move you in different parts and make you go on different adventures, and you can’t do that without dynamics.
